comparisonDesign.method: Synthetic loopback HTTP against the real Express app and migrated PostgreSQL. Authentication validates persisted hashed sessions through requireAuth; password login is not exercised. First-process samples use a fresh API process per request, with warm database pages and process imports excluded. Warm requests mix surfaces, profiles and two sessions per profile under a bounded shared concurrency. Client timing includes response-body receipt; server timing includes authentication and serialization. Active-pool interval samples are observations, not individual query wait times. No Nginx, TLS, browser rendering, external API or production load is measured.
comparisonDesign.workload: Distributed RDOs across two group members, equivalent synthetic volumes. One CPU/768 MiB PostgreSQL 16, eight API connections, shared concurrency four, view=summary.
comparisonDesign.counts: 832 measured 200 responses and eight expected access negatives per cohort; 800 warm responses (100 per route/profile), eight fresh-process samples, eight warmups, 16 post-write reads.
comparisonDesign.sourceParity: Eight complete outputs compared against baseline in separate Node processes on identical rows, after Decimal/Map/Set JSON normalization; repeated after role-name/salary/report-hour writes.
comparisonDesign.sourceParityFixture: Two overlapping point imports with reversed summary-row creation order; distributed RDOs, outside-point collaborator in both members, role history and role without cost profile, planned role hours, day/night, group/division.
comparisonDesign.latencyInterpretation: Sequential, not randomized replicated trials. API host not isolated; a much slower reference was retained. No global/causal p95 improvement attributed to two removed queries.
comparisonDesign.refreshTimeOrigin: After writes acknowledged and sampling phase prepared, not exact database commit timestamp; immediate card freshness not asserted.

limitations: Stable gain: point HTTP database-call median 38 to 36 (5.3%) in both accepted candidate cohorts; unchanged payload bytes. Direct attendance/diagnostic/calculation saves one Import read.
No accepted source-admission policy or new application queue. Rejected prototypes retained only as evidence.
Final confirmation no-queue fraction 26.6% to 29.1%, still far below 95%; peak pg waiting 41 to 43. No observed waiting sequence above five seconds.
Final individual admin detail p95 was slower than reference, while other targets varied. Earlier reference had much higher latency, retained rather than used for a speedup claim.
One cold sample per route/profile; no cold p95 or general cold target acceptance. No published/browser/LCP/operational 24h/seven-day acceptance.
Pool samples depend on event loop timing and do not measure individual query wait. Query peaks count submitted unfinished calls, including pool waiting.
nextLocalWork: Remove redundant work/reads and shorten source critical paths with unchanged financial/access/freshness rules. Do not adopt naive concurrency caps that merely move pool queueing to application and worsen total HTTP latency.
